question: Can one machine-state checkpoint carry several exact direct-dependency values and advance the bounded half-memory attack farther than the memo entries it displaces?

algorithm.entry: store one 32-bit stop, four 16-bit word identities, four 64-bit exact values, alignment padding, eight 64-bit VM registers, and one 64-bit accumulator in 120 bytes
algorithm.values: capture the requested target, first direct read, second direct read/write, and sequential write from the current exact replay step; duplicate identities collapse in insertion order
algorithm.index: write by target_word modulo checkpoint_capacity; lookup scans every small-table entry and chooses the latest strictly earlier stop containing the requested word
algorithm.accounting: all bundle bytes displace packed memo entries inside the same half-scratch arena; every scanned entry increments checkpoint_probes
algorithm.safety: stored values and machine state arise only from completed exact replay; exhaustion emits no proof

matched_target_checkpoint_baseline.comparison: the four-value policy displaces 32 memo entries and advances 55 additional primary iterations

partial_standard_holdout.interruption: seed index 3 was operator-stopped after several minutes without a result; seeds 4 through 7 were not run
partial_standard_holdout.interpretation: the seed-zero record is real but the fixed policy is not a general cross-seed improvement, and the replay-iteration ceiling does not bound memo/checkpoint call work

gate_mapping.reason: the seed-zero prefix record improves slightly but no proof completes, the cross-seed observation is mixed and incomplete, total call/probe work lacks an independent bound, and physical memory is unmeasured

next_use: add a deterministic total-operation ceiling and explain which rare bundle hits reduce depth before any broader retention policy or physical-host measurement
